Let $h>0$, let $I_i=[ih,(i+1)h)$, let $x_i=(i+\tfrac12)h$ be its center, and write $x_{i+1/2}=(i+1)h$ and $x_{i-1/2}=ih$ for its right and left faces. A **cell average** of a locally integrable scalar function $u$ is $U_i=h^{-1}\int_{I_i}u(x)\,dx$. The cells are half-open only to form a partition; the choice of endpoint representatives does not change an integral.

Here **MUSCL/minmod** means the piecewise-linear reconstruction with the limiter defined next; **nodal ENO2** means the two-stencil quadratic selector defined below; and **cell-average WENO5-JS/WENO-Z** means the three-candidate reconstructions with the normalized nonlinear weights displayed below. These names specify the constructions and do not, by themselves, assert an accuracy or stability property.

For real $a,b$, define
$$\operatorname{minmod}(a,b)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{sgn}(a)\min(|a|,|b|),&ab>0,\\0,&ab\le0.\end{cases}$$
The **MUSCL/minmod reconstruction** assigns the cell slope $s_i=h^{-1}\operatorname{minmod}(U_i-U_{i-1},U_{i+1}-U_i)$ and the two face states $U_{i-1/2}^{+,M}=U_i-hs_i/2$ and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,M}=U_i+hs_i/2$. Here $+$ denotes a trace from the right cell and $-$ a trace from the left cell.

For separate **nodal** data $V_j=u(y_j)$ at $y_j=jh$, define the second divided difference by $[y_a,y_b,y_c]V=(((V_c-V_b)/(y_c-y_b))-((V_b-V_a)/(y_b-y_a)))/(y_c-y_a)$. At the face $y_{i+1/2}=(i+\tfrac12)h$, set $d_L=|[y_{i-1},y_i,y_{i+1}]V|$ and $d_R=|[y_i,y_{i+1},y_{i+2}]V|$. Choose the left triple when $d_L\le d_R$ and otherwise choose the right triple. For the selected triple $(y_a,y_b,y_c)$ define its Newton quadratic by
$$P_{a,b,c}(y)=V_a+\frac{V_b-V_a}{y_b-y_a}(y-y_a)+[y_a,y_b,y_c]V\,(y-y_a)(y-y_b).$$
The **nodal ENO2 face value** is $P_{a,b,c}(y_{i+1/2})$. This nodal interpolation branch is distinct from the cell-average WENO branch below.

For cell averages $U_{i-2},\ldots,U_{i+2}$, define the left-biased WENO5 candidate face functionals
$$p_0=(2U_{i-2}-7U_{i-1}+11U_i)/6,\qquad p_1=(-U_{i-1}+5U_i+2U_{i+1})/6,\qquad p_2=(2U_i+5U_{i+1}-U_{i+2})/6.$$
Define the Jiang–Shu indicators
$$\beta_0=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-2}-2U_{i-1}+U_i)^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-2}-4U_{i-1}+3U_i)^2,$$
$$\beta_1=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-1}-2U_i+U_{i+1})^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-1}-U_{i+1})^2,\qquad \beta_2=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_i-2U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2+\tfrac14(3U_i-4U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2.$$
Fix a positive parameter $\epsilon_0$ with the same units as each $\beta_k$, independently of $h$, and ideal weights $(d_0,d_1,d_2)=(1/10,6/10,3/10)$. If $u$ is nondimensionalized, $\epsilon_0$ is a fixed positive number. The **WENO-JS weights** and left face value are $\alpha_k^J=d_k/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k)^2$, $\omega_k^J=\alpha_k^J/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^J$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,J}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Jp_k$. For the **WENO-Z comparison**, use the fifth-order $p=2$ weights: with $\tau_5=|\beta_0-\beta_2|$, set $\alpha_k^Z=d_k[1+(\tau_5/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k))^2]$, $\omega_k^Z=\alpha_k^Z/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^Z$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,Z}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Zp_k$. All denominators are positive because $\epsilon_0>0$ and every $\beta_k$ is a sum of squares. The right face state is obtained by reflection about that face: replace each stencil value $U_k$ in the displayed left formula by $U_{2i+1-k}$.

For scalar linear advection $u_t+a u_x=0$, a **direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update** uses $\nu=a\Delta t/h$, the flux $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{-,M}$ when $a\ge0$ and $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{+,M}$ when $a<0$, and $U_i^{n+1}=U_i^n-(\Delta t/h)(F_{i+1/2}-F_{i-1/2})$. For a vector system whose flux Jacobian at an interface is diagonalizable as $A=R\Lambda R^{-1}$ with real diagonal $\Lambda$, a **characteristic-wise reconstruction** applies a chosen scalar reconstruction to the components of $R^{-1}U$ and maps the reconstructed vector back by $R$. For $p_1$, $(-1,5,2)$ has dot products $6$, $0$, and $0$ with $(1,1,1)$, $(-3/2,-1/2,1/2)$, and $(7/3,1/3,1/3)$. For $p_2$, $(2,5,-1)$ has dot products $6$, $0$, and $0$ with $(1,1,1)$, $(-1/2,1/2,3/2)$, and $(1/3,1/3,7/3)$. After division by $6$, each candidate exactly reproduces $1,z,z^2$ at the face. The degree-two Taylor polynomial at $x_{i+1/2}$ therefore cancels from $p_k-u(x_{i+1/2})$. By [F2], the pointwise remainder on each stencil is bounded by $M_3(3h)^3/3!$, where $M_3=\sup|u'''|$; averaging preserves this bound. Let $h>0$, let $I_i=[ih,(i+1)h)$, let $x_i=(i+\tfrac12)h$ be its center, and write $x_{i+1/2}=(i+1)h$ and $x_{i-1/2}=ih$ for its right and left faces. A **cell average** of a locally integrable scalar function $u$ is $U_i=h^{-1}\int_{I_i}u(x)\,dx$. The cells are half-open only to form a partition; the choice of endpoint representatives does not change an integral.

Here **MUSCL/minmod** means the piecewise-linear reconstruction with the limiter defined next; **nodal ENO2** means the two-stencil quadratic selector defined below; and **cell-average WENO5-JS/WENO-Z** means the three-candidate reconstructions with the normalized nonlinear weights displayed below. These names specify the constructions and do not, by themselves, assert an accuracy or stability property.

For real $a,b$, define
$$\operatorname{minmod}(a,b)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{sgn}(a)\min(|a|,|b|),&ab>0,\\0,&ab\le0.\end{cases}$$
The **MUSCL/minmod reconstruction** assigns the cell slope $s_i=h^{-1}\operatorname{minmod}(U_i-U_{i-1},U_{i+1}-U_i)$ and the two face states $U_{i-1/2}^{+,M}=U_i-hs_i/2$ and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,M}=U_i+hs_i/2$. Here $+$ denotes a trace from the right cell and $-$ a trace from the left cell.

For separate **nodal** data $V_j=u(y_j)$ at $y_j=jh$, define the second divided difference by $[y_a,y_b,y_c]V=(((V_c-V_b)/(y_c-y_b))-((V_b-V_a)/(y_b-y_a)))/(y_c-y_a)$. At the face $y_{i+1/2}=(i+\tfrac12)h$, set $d_L=|[y_{i-1},y_i,y_{i+1}]V|$ and $d_R=|[y_i,y_{i+1},y_{i+2}]V|$. Choose the left triple when $d_L\le d_R$ and otherwise choose the right triple. For the selected triple $(y_a,y_b,y_c)$ define its Newton quadratic by
$$P_{a,b,c}(y)=V_a+\frac{V_b-V_a}{y_b-y_a}(y-y_a)+[y_a,y_b,y_c]V\,(y-y_a)(y-y_b).$$
The **nodal ENO2 face value** is $P_{a,b,c}(y_{i+1/2})$. This nodal interpolation branch is distinct from the cell-average WENO branch below.

For cell averages $U_{i-2},\ldots,U_{i+2}$, define the left-biased WENO5 candidate face functionals
$$p_0=(2U_{i-2}-7U_{i-1}+11U_i)/6,\qquad p_1=(-U_{i-1}+5U_i+2U_{i+1})/6,\qquad p_2=(2U_i+5U_{i+1}-U_{i+2})/6.$$
Define the Jiang–Shu indicators
$$\beta_0=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-2}-2U_{i-1}+U_i)^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-2}-4U_{i-1}+3U_i)^2,$$
$$\beta_1=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-1}-2U_i+U_{i+1})^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-1}-U_{i+1})^2,\qquad \beta_2=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_i-2U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2+\tfrac14(3U_i-4U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2.$$
Fix a positive parameter $\epsilon_0$ with the same units as each $\beta_k$, independently of $h$, and ideal weights $(d_0,d_1,d_2)=(1/10,6/10,3/10)$. If $u$ is nondimensionalized, $\epsilon_0$ is a fixed positive number. The **WENO-JS weights** and left face value are $\alpha_k^J=d_k/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k)^2$, $\omega_k^J=\alpha_k^J/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^J$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,J}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Jp_k$. For the **WENO-Z comparison**, use the fifth-order $p=2$ weights: with $\tau_5=|\beta_0-\beta_2|$, set $\alpha_k^Z=d_k[1+(\tau_5/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k))^2]$, $\omega_k^Z=\alpha_k^Z/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^Z$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,Z}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Zp_k$. All denominators are positive because $\epsilon_0>0$ and every $\beta_k$ is a sum of squares. The right face state is obtained by reflection about that face: replace each stencil value $U_k$ in the displayed left formula by $U_{2i+1-k}$.

For scalar linear advection $u_t+a u_x=0$, a **direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update** uses $\nu=a\Delta t/h$, the flux $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{-,M}$ when $a\ge0$ and $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{+,M}$ when $a<0$, and $U_i^{n+1}=U_i^n-(\Delta t/h)(F_{i+1/2}-F_{i-1/2})$. The total variation of a sequence is $\operatorname{TV}(U)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}|U_{i+1}-U_i|$ when the sum is finite; **TVD** means that this quantity does not increase in one update.

For a vector system whose flux Jacobian at an interface is diagonalizable as $A=R\Lambda R^{-1}$ with real diagonal $\Lambda$, a **characteristic-wise reconstruction** applies a chosen scalar reconstruction to the components of $R^{-1}U$ and maps the reconstructed vector back by $R$. This definition alone gives no TVD or stability result for systems.

Let $h>0$, let $I_j=[jh,(j+1)h)$, and let $x_{i+1/2}=(i+1)h$. For $u\in C^5$ on the union of cells $I_{i-2},\ldots,I_{i+2}$, let $p_0,p_1,p_2$ be the cell-average functionals in [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]]. Each candidate reproduces every polynomial of degree at most two exactly at $x_{i+1/2}$. The ideal combination $p_{opt}=p_0/10+3p_1/5+3p_2/10$ reproduces every polynomial of degree at most four and satisfies $|p_{opt}-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le (23/15)(3^5/5!)\,\sup|u^{(5)}|\,h^5$. Each candidate separately satisfies $|p_k-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le15\sup|u'''|h^3$.

Let $u\in C^2$ on a neighborhood of a cell and its two neighbors, and suppose $|u'(x)|\ge c>0$ there. Let $U_j$ be the averages of $u$ over uniform cells of width $h$, centered at $x_j=x_0+jh$. For sufficiently small $h$, the MUSCL/minmod face states of [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]] satisfy
$$|U_i+hs_i/2-u(x_i+h/2)|\le C h^2,\qquad |U_i-hs_i/2-u(x_i-h/2)|\le C h^2,$$
where $C$ depends only on $c$ and a bound for $|u''|$ on the stated neighborhood.

Let $u\in C^5$ on the five-cell stencil, let $\sup|u'''|<\infty$ and $\sup|u^{(5)}|<\infty$, and let $\epsilon_0>0$ be fixed independently of $h$. For the cell-average WENO-JS and WENO-Z states in [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]], there is a constant $C$ independent of sufficiently small $h$ such that
$$|U_{i+1/2}^{-,J}-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le Ch^5,\qquad |U_{i+1/2}^{-,Z}-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le Ch^5.$$
The same result holds for the reflected right states.

derivations.claim: Since the average of an affine function over a cell equals its value at the cell center, $U_i^n=x_i-at_n$. Hence $U_i^n-U_{i-1}^n=U_{i+1}^n-U_i^n=h$ and the minmod slope is $s_i=1$. The right MUSCL trace is $U_i^n+h/2=(i+1)h-at_n=u(x_{i+1/2},t_n)$, with the reflected left trace giving the same exact value at the face.

The WENO candidates reproduce affine polynomials by [F2], so $p_0=p_1=p_2=u(x_{i+1/2},t_n)$. Each normalized weight triple therefore returns this same exact value. The uniform smooth profile also satisfies [F3] and [F4], with zero error here because it is affine.

For $a>0$, the upwind flux is $a((i+1)h-at_n)$ and the left face flux is $a(ih-at_n)$; their difference is $ah$, so the update gives $U_i^{n+1}=x_i-at_n-a\Delta t$, the exact average at $t_{n+1}$. For $a<0$ the reflected right trace yields the same interface value and flux difference; for $a=0$ both the flux and time change vanish.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $u$ be an almost-everywhere equivalence class of measurable functions on
$\mathbb R$ with $u\in L^\infty(\mathbb R)\cap L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$,
using the quotient convention of
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], the essentially bounded
class of [[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]], and the local integrability
convention of [[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]]. For $h>0$ define
$$D_hu(x):=u(x+h)-u(x),\qquad \operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{tr}}(u):=\sup_{h>0}\frac1h\int_{\mathbb R}|D_hu(x)|\,dx,$$
where the integral may be $+\infty$. The **bounded BV class on the line**
$\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ consists of those classes for which
$\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{tr}}(u)<\infty$; we write
$\operatorname{TV}(u):=\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{tr}}(u)$.

This translation-variation convention is the standard one-dimensional BV
seminorm on bounded locally integrable classes. It is unchanged by modifying
$u$ on a null set, because each translate of a null set is null. It does not
require $u\in L^1(\mathbb R)$: every bounded constant function belongs to
$\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ and has variation $0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $T>0$,
$f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, and $u_0\in\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ in the sense of
[[def-bounded-bv-data-on-line]]. Put
$I=[\operatorname*{ess\,inf}u_0,\operatorname*{ess\,sup}u_0]$. Let
$F\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be locally Lipschitz, consistent with $f$,
nondecreasing in its first coordinate and nonincreasing in its second on
$I^2$, with coordinate Lipschitz bounds $L_1,L_2$ as in
[[def-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-scheme]]. For a family of meshes
$(h_m,\tau_m)$ assume
$$h_m,\tau_m\to0,\qquad \frac{\tau_m}{h_m}(L_1+L_2)\le1,\qquad \frac{\tau_m}{h_m}\ge c_*>0.$$
For each mesh, initialize by cell averages and update with the shared flux $F$.
Let $W_m$ be the piecewise-linear time interpolant and $\mathcal U_m$ the
piecewise-constant state reconstruction. If $u_0\in L^1(\mathbb R)$, assume
Dependent Choice $\mathrm{DC}$ in addition to $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; no DC
assumption is made when $u_0\notin L^1(\mathbb R)$.

Then there is a unique bounded Kruzhkov entropy solution $u$ on
$\mathbb R\times(0,T)$ with initial datum $u_0$, and
$$W_m\longrightarrow u\quad\text{in }C([0,T];L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)),\qquad \mathcal U_m\longrightarrow u\quad\text{strongly in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R\times(0,T)).$$
For nonintegrable bounded BV data, existence is obtained from the local
finite-volume limit in the proof before local contraction gives uniqueness.
The theorem claims local convergence; global $L^1$ convergence requires
additional uniform tail control. The time-to-space lower bound $c_*$ is retained
from the approved convergence interface, and no system-valued or non-BV
entropy-process conclusion is asserted.

Let $n\ge1$, $T>0$, $f\in C^1(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^n)$, and
$\Pi_T=\mathbb R^n\times(0,T)$. The unknown and initial datum are equivalence
classes $[u]\in L^\infty(\Pi_T)$ and
$[u_0]\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$, where
equality is Lebesgue-a.e. ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]]).

For $k\in\mathbb R$ define the **Kruzhkov entropy pair**
$$\eta_k(s)=|s-k|,\qquad q_k(s)=\operatorname{sgn}(s-k)\bigl(f(s)-f(k)\bigr),$$
with $\operatorname{sgn}(0)=0$ ([[def-abs-value]]). Then $\eta_k$ is convex
and $q_k'=\eta_k'f'$ almost everywhere, so $(\eta_k,q_k)$ is a locally Lipschitz convex
entropy--entropy flux pair ([[def-convex-entropy-entropy-flux-pair]]).

The class $[u]$ is a **Kruzhkov entropy solution** of
$u_t+\operatorname{div}_x f(u)=0$ with initial trace $[u_0]$ if:

(i) for every $k\in\mathbb R$ and every nonnegative
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Pi_T)$,
$$\int_{\Pi_T}\bigl(\eta_k(u)\,\varphi_t+q_k(u)\cdot\nabla_x\varphi\bigr)\,dx\,dt\ge0,$$
that is, $\partial_t\eta_k(u)+\operatorname{div}_x q_k(u)\le0$ in
$\mathcal D'(\Pi_T)$; and

(ii) for every compact $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$,
$$\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0<t<\min\{\delta,T\}}\int_K|u(t,x)-u_0(x)|\,dx=0.$$

The integral in (i) is independent of the representative because its integrand
is unchanged almost everywhere. For (ii), Fubini's theorem gives locally
integrable spatial sections for almost every $t$
([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]); the
displayed slice integral is defined for those times and its essential supremum
ignores the exceptional null set. If $u$ or $u_0$ is changed on a null set in
its respective space, Fubini's theorem shows that the slice-integral function
changes only for a null set of times, so the trace condition is well defined on
the equivalence classes: this is the **strong local $L^1$ initial trace**.

Taking $k$ above and below the essential range of $u$ makes $\eta_k$ equal
$k-u$ and $u-k$, whose $t$- and $x$-derivatives cancel the constant terms
against compactly supported test functions, so the entropy inequalities imply
the weak conservation law of
[[def-distributional-weak-solution-of-a-scalar-conservation-law]] tested
against nonnegative test functions, hence by linearity against all test
functions.

To recover the Cauchy boundary term, apply the interior weak identity to
$\varphi(t,x)\zeta(t/\delta)$, where $\zeta$ is smooth and nondecreasing,
$\zeta=0$ on $(-\infty,1/2]$ and $\zeta=1$ on $[1,\infty)$.

derivations.claim:
First suppose $a>0$. If $d_i\ne0$, then $m_i/d_i$ and $m_{i-1}/d_i$ lie in $[0,1]$: in each minmod, $d_i$ is one argument, so a nonzero output has the sign of $d_i$ and magnitude at most $|d_i|$. Set
$$C_i=\mu\left[1+\frac{m_i/d_i-m_{i-1}/d_i}{2}\right]$$
in this case. If $d_i=0$, then $m_i=m_{i-1}=0$; set $C_i=\mu$. In either case $\mu/2\le C_i\le3\mu/2$, and the exact update satisfies $U_i^+=U_i-C_id_i=(1-C_i)U_i+C_iU_{i-1}$. Thus $0\le C_i\le1$ when $\mu\le2/3$, including equality.

Subtract the identity for $U_{i-1}^+$ in step 1.1 from that for $U_i^+$ to obtain $d_i^+=(1-C_i)d_i+C_{i-1}d_{i-1}$. The coefficients are nonnegative, so $|d_i^+|\le(1-C_i)|d_i|+C_{i-1}|d_{i-1}|$. For periodic data, $C_i$ is $N$-periodic because it is defined from shifts of $U$; summing over one period and cyclically reindexing gives $\operatorname{TV}_N(U^+)\le\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}[(1-C_i)+C_i]|d_i|=\operatorname{TV}_N(U)$. This also covers $N=1$, when every $d_i=0$. For bi-infinite data, both nonnegative series on the right are bounded by $\sum_i|d_i|<\infty$. Reindexing the absolutely convergent second series gives $\operatorname{TV}(U^+)\le\sum_i[(1-C_i)+C_i]|d_i|=\operatorname{TV}(U)$, so the updated sequence still has finite variation.

Now suppose $a<0$. At face $i+1/2$, [F2] gives $F_{i+1/2}=a(U_{i+1}-m_{i+1}/2)$ and $F_{i-1/2}=a(U_i-m_i/2)$, hence $U_i^+=U_i+\mu[(U_{i+1}-U_i)-(m_{i+1}-m_i)/2]$. Reflect the data by $V_j=U_{-j}$. Its minmod increments obey $m_j^V=-m_{-j}$, because reflection reverses each adjacent difference and minmod is odd under simultaneous sign reversal. With $i=-j$, the positive-speed expression for $V_j$ is $V_j-\mu[(V_j-V_{j-1})+(m_j^V-m_{j-1}^V)/2]=U_i+\mu[(U_{i+1}-U_i)-(m_{i+1}-m_i)/2]$, exactly the negative-speed update just computed. Also $V_j-V_{j-1}=-(U_{-j+1}-U_{-j})$, so reflection only reindexes the absolute increments and preserves both the bi-infinite and periodic variation sums. Step 2.1 therefore proves the claim for negative velocity. If $a=0$, both fluxes vanish; if $\Delta t=0$, their difference is multiplied by zero in the update. In either case the update is the identity, covering $\mu=0$.

Fix $2/3<\mu\le1$, any $h>0$ and any $a\ne0$, and take $\Delta t=\mu h/|a|$. For positive velocity choose $U_{-1}=U_1=1/2$, $U_0=1$, and $U_i=0$ otherwise; its initial variation is $|1/2|+|1/2|+|{-1/2}|+|{-1/2}|=2$. The only nonzero differences are $d_{-1}=d_0=1/2$ and $d_1=d_2=-1/2$, so the only nonzero minmod increments are $m_{-1}=1/2$ and $m_1=-1/2$. Substituting these in [F2], the four affected updates are $U_{-1}^+=1/2-\mu(1/2+1/4)=A$, $U_0^+=1-\mu(1/2-1/4)=B$, $U_1^+=1/2-\mu(-1/2-1/4)=C$, and $U_2^+=0-\mu(-1/2+1/4)=D$, where $A=1/2-3\mu/4$, $B=1-\mu/4$, $C=1/2+3\mu/4$, and $D=\mu/4$; every other update is zero because its state and all adjacent minmod increments are zero. Here $A<0$, $B\ge3/4>0$, $C-B=\mu-1/2>0$, $D>0$, and $C-D=1/2+\mu/2>0$, so $A<0<B<C$ and $0<D<C$. Hence $\operatorname{TV}(U^+)= -A+(B-A)+(C-B)+(C-D)+D=2(C-A)=3\mu>2$. For negative velocity reflect this witness; step 3.1 preserves its updated variation. Periodizing the data with any $N\ge7$ leaves at least four zero initial cells between successive three-cell supports and at least three zero updated entries between the four affected entries; since a positive-velocity update uses only cells $i-2,\ldots,i+1$ and a negative-velocity update uses only cells $i-1,\ldots,i+2$, no stencil meets two distinct support copies, and the periodic variation is the same $3\mu$.
